learn.title: Solar PV and the Photoelectric Effect
learn.intro: Solar photovoltaic (PV) panels convert sunlight directly into electricity using the photoelectric effect, a phenomenon that won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921. Understanding how this works is key to appreciating solar energy's role in reducing carbon emissions and powering homes sustainably.
learn.c1_text: Each solar cell has a top layer of phosphorus-doped (negative) silicon and a bottom layer of boron-doped (positive) silicon. This creates an electric field that pushes freed electrons in one direction, generating direct current (DC) electricity.
learn.c3_text: India ranks 3rd globally in solar capacity with over 70 GW installed by 2023. The Bhadla Solar Park in Rajasthan spans 14,000 acres and generates enough power for 150,000 homes, showcasing India’s aggressive push under the International Solar Alliance.
learn.stat3: Silicon solar cells are ~20% efficient on average
learn.stat4: One ton of CO₂ saved per MWh of solar generated

learn.title: Solid-State Batteries Explained
learn.intro: Solid-state batteries replace liquid electrolytes with solids, offering higher energy density and improved safety. They could revolutionize electric vehicles and grid storage by enabling faster charging, longer life, and reduced fire risks compared to traditional lithium-ion batteries.
learn.c1_text: Traditional lithium-ion batteries use a liquid electrolyte that can leak or catch fire. Solid-state batteries swap this for a ceramic or polymer solid, making them safer and more compact. It’s like replacing water in a hose with pressurized air—cleaner and less prone to bursts.
learn.c2_text: Solid-state batteries can store up to 50% more energy per unit weight than conventional ones. This means EVs could travel 500+ miles on a single charge instead of 250–300 miles today. The denser packing also allows for lighter, smaller battery packs without sacrificing range.
learn.c3_text: India launched its National Mission on Advanced and High-Impact Technologies (MAIT) to boost domestic battery manufacturing. Startups like Ather Energy are testing solid-state prototypes, aiming to reduce reliance on imports and support the goal of 30% EV adoption by 2030.
learn.stat1: Solid-state batteries offer 2x energy density vs Li-ion
learn.stat2: EV range may increase to 500+ miles with solid-state
learn.stat3: Battery fires account for <0.01% of EV incidents

learn.title: Green Hydrogen via Water Electrolysis
learn.intro: Green hydrogen is produced by splitting water using renewable electricity, offering a clean fuel alternative for hard-to-electrify sectors like steelmaking and shipping. Two main technologies—PEM and alkaline electrolysis—are shaping the future of this versatile energy carrier.
learn.c1_text: Electrolysis uses electricity to split water (H₂O) into hydrogen (H₂) and oxygen (O₂). If powered by renewables, it's called 'green' hydrogen. Imagine using solar power to make fuel from seawater—an inexhaustible source that emits only water when burned.
learn.c2_text: PEM electrolyzers use rare metals but respond quickly to variable power, ideal for pairing with wind/solar. Alkaline systems are cheaper and use abundant materials but operate at lower pressures. Both produce pure H₂ but differ in cost, efficiency, and scalability for industrial use.
learn.c3_text: India launched a $2.3 billion National Green Hydrogen Mission in 2023, targeting 5 Mton/year production by 2030. Reliance Industries plans a $10B investment in green hydrogen, including a mega plant in Gujarat powered entirely by offshore wind and solar.
learn.stat1: Global green H₂ demand projected to hit 50 Mton by 2050
learn.stat3: India aims for 5 Mton/year green H₂ by 2030
learn.stat4: Water needed: 9 L per kg of H₂ produced

learn.title: Offshore Wind Farms Explained
learn.intro: Offshore wind farms harness stronger, steadier winds over oceans, delivering massive amounts of clean electricity. With floating turbines expanding into deeper waters, these installations are becoming vital for coastal nations seeking reliable, large-scale renewable energy.
learn.c1_text: Offshore winds blow harder and more consistently than land-based ones. A single modern turbine can generate enough electricity for 6,000 homes annually. Think of it as placing your windmill in a river versus the ocean—the latter just has more force behind it.
learn.c2_text: Turbines are mounted on fixed or floating foundations driven into the seabed. Cables bury underground to connect to substations, then transmit power via underwater cables to shore. It’s like building a highway system beneath the waves to deliver energy directly to cities.
learn.c3_text: India has identified 338 GW potential in offshore wind along its 7,500 km coastline. The government approved the country’s first commercial offshore project off Tamil Nadu in 2023, targeting 30 GW by 2030 with investments exceeding $100 billion.
learn.stat3: India targets 30 GW offshore wind by 2030
learn.stat4: Floating turbines can go 600+ meters deep

learn.title: Floating Solar Farms on Water
learn.intro: Floating solar farms install PV arrays on reservoirs, lakes, and lagoons, saving land while boosting performance. These innovative projects reduce evaporation, improve panel cooling, and open new frontiers for solar deployment in densely populated regions.
learn.c1_text: By placing solar panels on water bodies, countries avoid competing for scarce land. Over 12 GW of floating PV was installed globally by 2023. It’s like turning unused rooftops upside down—using space you weren’t even utilizing before.
learn.c2_text: Water cools solar panels naturally, increasing output by up to 10%. Less heat degradation means longer lifespans and better returns. Like wearing a wet hat on a hot day, floating panels stay cooler and work smarter thanks to their aquatic environment.
learn.c3_text: India has over 40 floating solar projects underway, including a 150 MW plant on the Rihand Dam. The government promotes floatsolar under its National Solar Mission, aiming to conserve water while adding 40 GW floating capacity by 2030 across 100+ water bodies.
learn.stat1: Over 12 GW global floating PV installed (2023)
learn.stat2: Cooling increases panel output by up to 10%
learn.stat3: India plans 40 GW floating solar by 2030
learn.stat4: Floating PV reduces evaporation by up to 30%

learn.title: Types of Solar Inverters Explained
learn.intro: Solar inverters convert DC power from panels into usable AC power for homes and grids. Choosing the right type—string, micro, or hybrid—affects performance, cost, and flexibility. Each serves different needs, from simple rooftops to smart energy management systems.
learn.c1_text: String inverters connect multiple panels in series, converting DC to AC at one central point. Like linking Christmas lights together, if one goes out, the whole string dims. Best for shade-free roofs, they’re affordable but limit individual panel monitoring.
learn.c2_text: Hybrid inverters manage both solar input and battery storage, acting as a traffic cop for energy flow. They decide whether excess power charges batteries or feeds the grid. Ideal for homeowners wanting backup power and self-consumption optimization in one device.
learn.c3_text: India targets 40 GW rooftop solar by 2022 (now extended). Microinverters gain traction in urban areas like Mumbai and Delhi where rooftop shading is common. Startups like Tata Power and Loom Solar offer hybrid-ready solutions tailored for Indian grid conditions and frequent outages.
learn.stat2: Microinverters improve yield by 5–25% in shaded conditions
learn.stat3: India targets 40 GW rooftop solar capacity
